description: Minimum set of CI gate steps every workflow must keep running, enforced by scripts/check_ci_integrity.py in .github/workflows/workflow-integrity.yml. Deleting one of these steps cannot fail CI by itself - a removed step reports nothing - so the gate checks this list instead. Retiring a gate deliberately is allowed: move its name out of must_have and into retired, with a reason, in the same pull request, so the deletion is in the diff. Consolidating a job into another one is allowed the same way: record the old job id under moved with its destination and a reason, and every step that job was required to run is then enforced in the destination instead - a move that loses a step fails exactly like a deletion.

contract: Error codes and registry wiring are consistent
Error-surface table is up to date
Assert wasm artifact is present and non-empty
frontend: Differential vectors are up to date
Testnet canary suite (imports the frontend builders)
data-plane: Event registry artifacts are up to date
Event compatibility check against the base
Error catalog is up to date
docs: Tracked files are stored with LF

tamper-audit: Report the pinned signing key fingerprint
verify-release: Download the published Wasm and attestation
Cross-check the release asset against the in-repo mirror
Verify the signature and the digest

fuzz: Restore corpus from the fuzz-corpus branch
report: Combine per-target runs into one report
Persist corpus and report to fuzz-corpus

terraform: Structural + hardening checks on the rendered artifacts
Caddyfile validates in the image the stack actually runs
No plaintext secrets anywhere in the rendered output

rollback: Roll back to the previously promoted digest

wasm: Verify the build is reproducible (double build, wasm + spec-json)
Compute digest and emit toolchain release metadata
Mirror the signed attestation into attestations/

integrity: Self-test: the checker can still fail
Self-test: the source scanner can still fail
Workflows parse and every step is well-formed
Every required CI gate is still wired
No text file is committed as UTF-16 or with a BOM
Every tracked source file is still a parseable program

devcontainer-verify.reason: Its whole purpose was a red that survives a formatting failure in the contract job, so that a compile error reads differently from a rustfmt complaint. The steps now run inside contract under `if: ${{ always() && !cancelled() }}`, which preserves that: they still execute when the job already failed at Format check or Clippy. One check instead of two, same diagnostic separation.

cli-parity.reason: The frontend job already installs this same tools/streampay-cli tree (`Install CLI dependencies for cross-client parity`) and runs the parity suite against it; the separate job existed only to have its own check run. Folded so the wire-parity result travels with the app it mirrors.

event-registry.reason: The registry, the schemas and the TypeScript types are the contract's wire format, and indexer/reconciler/ttl-sentinel/perf-budgets are its consumers. One job owns the producer and every consumer, so a PR that changes an event shape sees the drift in the same check that reports the consumer breakage.

indexer.reason: Consumer of the event registry; folded into the job that gates the schema it reads. Its own working-directory is inlined per step, so `npm ci` still runs against indexer/package-lock.json.

reconciler.reason: Consumer of the indexer's output and the contract events; same merge as indexer, with reconciler's working-directory inlined per step.

ttl-sentinel.reason: The sentinel reads contract storage constants and emits the same event shapes the registry owns, so it belongs with the wire-format checks. infra/ttl-sentinel working-directory is inlined per step.

perf-budgets.reason: Builds and measures the indexer, which data-plane already builds; the budget numbers are only meaningful against that tree, and the error-catalog freshness gate is a derived-artifact check like the event registry's.

benchmarks.reason: Protocol comparison over the same contract build, with no baseline-comparison isolation requirement, so it shares the data-plane runner instead of paying for another checkout and toolchain install.
